answer_text: Oxides of metals such as CaO are basic and turn red litmus blue, while oxides of non-metals such as CO2 are acidic and turn blue litmus red. Calcium oxide is an ionic solid. When it is molten the Ca2+ and O2- ions can move, so it conducts electricity. In the solid the ions are locked in the lattice, and carbon dioxide is a covalent molecule with no ions at all, so neither solid CaO nor CO2 gas conducts.
